# Run and maintain your standalone application

This package includes the original React/Vite application, entity schemas, backend handlers, agents, binary assets, and an independent Node.js/SQLite runtime. The application uses its own server instead of the Base44 backend. The original source archive is not a database backup.

## Localhost

Install Node.js 24 LTS, version 24.12 or newer within the 24 series. From this directory:

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env`: set `ADMIN_EMAIL` and a unique `ADMIN_PASSWORD` of at least 12 characters. Then:

```sh
npm run build
npm start
```

Open **http://localhost:3000** and sign in with those credentials. The first startup creates the administrator; changing these environment values later does not reset an existing account. For editing with hot reload, use `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:5173. The Vite proxy sends API and realtime traffic to the same local backend.

Use `npm run test:standalone` to check access rules, local accounts and data migration. S4-specific integration checks run when that app's modules are present. Tests use temporary records and databases. The migration report initially marks build/runtime verification as not run; a downloaded export has not executed your application.

## Custom domain

Choose your hostname when exporting, or update `standalone/Caddyfile` afterward. Point its DNS A/AAAA records to your server, allow ports 80 and 443, and set `PUBLIC_URL=https://your.hostname` in `.env`.

```sh
docker compose --profile domain up --build -d
```

Caddy obtains HTTPS certificates and proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to the app. For local Docker use, `docker compose up --build -d app` exposes http://localhost:3000. The Docker configuration requires Docker Compose; it is provided as deployment source and must be verified on your host.

The `app_data` volume persists the SQLite database and uploads. On direct Node installations, these live in `data/` unless paths are configured. Back up the database **and** uploads together while the app is stopped, or use SQLite's online backup tooling. Keep `.env` private and outside source control. One running app process owns the database and collaboration rooms; this runtime does not implement distributed multi-instance collaboration.

## Accounts, records and uploaded files

Hosted passwords are not exported. New accounts use local password hashes and expiring sessions. Self-registration is disabled by default. Configure email delivery, then invite users from the app; existing imported User profiles are linked by email, preserving their IDs. Invited users create new passwords.

Obtain a separate authorized data export with this structure:

```json
{"entities":{"User":[{"id":"old-user-id","email":"person@example.com","role":"user"}],"YourModel":[{"id":"record-id","owner_id":"old-user-id"}]}}
```

With the standalone server running and administrator credentials set in `.env`:

```sh
node --env-file-if-exists=.env standalone/server/data.mjs import records.json
node --env-file-if-exists=.env standalone/server/data.mjs export backup.json
```

Imports run atomically, preserve record IDs, and remap references when an imported user email already has a local account. The current administrator retains its role. Import User records and related entities together when IDs need remapping. Existing local passwords are retained; password hashes from the hosted system are discarded. Split imports larger than 29 MB into smaller batches, starting with User records. These commands transfer records, not binary uploads. Migrate referenced files separately and update their URLs. The ZIP includes public platform assets that the exporter could fetch; see `missing_public_assets` in the report for any failures.

## AI models and external integrations

Set `AI_PROVIDER` to `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini` or `compatible`, plus `AI_MODEL` and `AI_API_KEY` (or the corresponding provider key). For an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `AI_BASE_URL`, for example `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`, and its served model name. In Docker, localhost refers to the container; use a reachable model-server address. The compatible adapter uses the chat-completions protocol. Arbitrary model protocols need an adapter.

`AI_MODEL` overrides old hosted model aliases. Internet-grounded search is not automatically supplied. Image generation and transcription require an OpenAI-compatible supported service configuration; missing integrations return configuration errors.

Set `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` for email. Other function-specific environment names are listed in `.env.example` and `migration/report.json`. OAuth connections must be authorized independently; configure application-scoped `CONNECTOR_<PROVIDER>_ACCESS_TOKEN` and, where needed, `CONNECTOR_<PROVIDER>_CONFIG` JSON. Automatic token refresh requires your own provider setup.

For S4, external employee sync uses `EMPLOYEE_SOURCE_URL` / `EMPLOYEE_SOURCE_API_KEY`; external attendance sync uses `ATTENDANCE_SOURCE_URL` / `ATTENDANCE_SOURCE_API_KEY` and optional `ATTENDANCE_SOURCE_AUTH_HEADER`. These adapters expect your configured service. Imported source contained hard-coded credentials: the exporter removed recognized key literals into environment variables and recorded their **names only**. Rotate the original keys before configuring replacements.

## Functions, automation and public routes

Backend handlers, entity access rules, agents and realtime rooms run on this server. A compatibility layer implements the APIs used by the imported source. This is an application migration, not a guarantee that every hosted-platform feature has identical behavior. Build the app, run tests, and exercise your actual business workflows before production use.

Functions require sign-in by default. Scheduled jobs, public portals, webhooks, and external email approval links need explicit setup. Set `PUBLIC_FUNCTIONS` only after adding and verifying the appropriate signature/token checks in each handler. Browser code cannot use the server's service-role client. Configure a scheduler separately for periodic tasks; source function files alone do not recreate hosted schedules. Browser extensions and Canva integrations keep their source and require their own build, registration and permissions.

Review `migration/report.json` for counts, exclusions, fixes, required settings and verification status. Private environment files, keys, local database files, dependency folders and git history are excluded from exports. Public callback examples and application-owned asset references are rewritten where supported; review custom hard-coded endpoints for your deployment.
